newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND TAKES OVERALL TITLE AS JAGGE WINS SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND TAKES OVERALL TITLE AS JAGGE WINS SLALOM.

text.p: Norway's Finn Christian Jagge won the last race of the World Cup season on Sunday but the biggest winner of the day was France's Luc Alphand, who was crowned World Cup overall champion after the men's slalom.

The 31-year-old Alphand, a spectator on the last day, registered an historic triumph when his only rival for the overall title, Kjetil Andre Aamodt of Norway, failed to finish first or second in the climactic slalom.
"There is lots of emotion," said Alphand, mobbed by teammates, coaches and friends in the finish area once the title was clinched.
"It's like a liberation just now. The last two weeks have been very hard, there has been great pressure," added Alphand, who also won the downhill and Super-G season titles.
Alphand became the first French overall champion since Jean-Claude Killy 29 years ago and is the first speed specialist ever to win the crown.
"I have all the cups in my hand and later I will think about it," he said.

Aamodt gave it a gallant try on Sunday, battling back after standing 16th in the first run. He skied the second fastest second leg saw his faint hope extinguished when Austrian Mario Reiter, the 15th of 21 skiers, bumped him out of second place. Aamodt, with a time of 1:39.01, eventually wound up in seventh.
"It was inevitable," said the 25-year-old Aamodt, who won the overall crown in 1994.
"I needed a miracle to be second today. Alphand won six races and I won only one this year. That's the most important thing -- to win races. He deserves it."

Jagge led by a comfortable 0.73 of a second after a blistering run through the 62-gate course on Vail Mountain. The Norwegian skied more carefully the second time down, and won with a combined time of one minute 37.94 seconds, 0.12 of a second faster than Austrian Thomas Stangassinger.
Italian star Alberto Tomba, hampered this season by injuries, skied a masterful second run to finish third in 1:38.19, three-tenths of a second better than Reiter.
Swiss giant slalom champion Michael von Gruenigen finished fifth ahead of Ole Christian Furuseth and Aamodt.
The victory boosted Jagge into third place in the final slalom standings behind champion Thomas Sykora of Austria, who finished ninth on Sunday, and second-placed Stangassinger.

Jagge sneaked past France's Sebastien Amiez into third place by just one point, 374-373. Amiez, slalom silver medallist at the world championships, missed a gate in his first run and skied back to complete the leg but finished 18th and last in the race.
Jagge said he was not disappointed at all the attention given to Alphand on the day of his only victory of the season.
"Today's winner is Luc Alphand," said Jagge. "This is the Finals and we're here to find the winner of the World Cup."
Alphand finished the season with 1,130 points, built upon four downhill and two Super-G victories. Aamodt had 1,096 points, 75 ahead of Austrian Josef Strobl.
